opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
"You are not from Galilee also, are you? Look and see that no prophet arises from Galilee."

That line comes from the Gospel of John, specifically John 7:52. It is spoken by the Pharisees during a tense moment, when people are beginning to question who Jesus really is:

“You are not from Galilee also, are you?
Look and see that no prophet arises from Galilee.”

On the surface, it sounds like a simple argument. But underneath, it reveals something deeper.

They had already decided what truth should look like.

They believed the Messiah must come from a certain place, in a certain way—fitting their expectations. Galilee, to them, was insignificant, unrefined, not where anything important should come from. So instead of asking, “Could this be from God?” they dismissed it immediately.

They failed to recognize what was right in front of them.

They tell others to “look and see,” but they themselves refuse to see. They are so certain in what they think they know that they cannot recognize what is right in front of them. The Pharisees were not lacking information—they were closed.

This ties directly into the earlier reflections.

God does not move according to human expectations.
He chose David, the overlooked shepherd.
He revealed Himself through Christ, born in humility, raised in a place people dismissed.

Again and again, God works through what seems unlikely.

The danger is not ignorance.
The danger is thinking we already understand how God must act.

This connects to what Jesus says in John 9:39:

“Those who think they see might become blind.”

At first, that can be difficult to understand. But it points to the same truth: it is possible to miss God entirely—even when He is right in front of you.

And that becomes the quiet warning in this passage:

Be careful not to decide in advance where God is allowed to be found.

Because He often shows up in the places we least expect—and in ways we are not prepared for.

The real question is not, “Does this fit what I expect?”
But, “Am I willing to see if God is here?”
